questions.question: Define thermal diffusivity / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Define thermal diffusivity. [K] / [CO2]
  • Thermal diffusivity is the measure of how rapidly heat is transferred through a material. It
  • depends on thermal conductivity, density, and specific heat capacity. It is expressed as K = k
  • / (ρCp).

questions.question: Define fundamental units. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define fundamental units. [K] / [CO1]
  • Fundamental units are bas ic physical units that are independent and cannot be derived from
  • other units. Examples include meter, kilogram, second, and kelvin.

questions.question: How to convert kelvin to celcius scale ? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• How to convert kelvin to celsius scale? [A] / [CO1]
  • The temperature in Celsius is obtained by subtracting 273.15 from t he Kelvin value. The
  • relation is °C = K − 273.15.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Viscosity an important property in food processing operations. Justify / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Viscosity is an important property in food processing operations. Justify. [E] / [CO4]
  • Viscosity represents the resistance of a fluid to flow. It plays a critical role in food processing
  • as it affects p umping, mixing, heat transfer, and texture. High viscosity materials require
  • more energy for processing and influence product quality.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write mass balance equation for steady state system. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Write mass balance equation for steady state system. [U] / [CO1]
  • In a steady state system, there is no accumulation of mass within the system. Therefore, the
  • mass entering the system is equal to the mass leaving the system, expressed as Input =
  • Output.

questions.question: Differentiate between coarse crushing and fine grinding. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between coarse crushing and fine grinding. [U] / [CO5]
  • Coarse crushing reduces materials into relativ ely larger fragments, whereas fine grinding
  • produces very small and uniform particles with increased surface area. Grinding requires
  • higher energy compared to crushing.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What happens to water during freezing? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What happens to water during freezing? [U] / [CO3]
  • During freezing, water is conver ted into ice crystals. This process leads to expansion in
  • volume and reduction in water activity. Large ice crystals may damage cellular structures in
  • food.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define ohmic heating. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Define ohmic heating. [U] / [CO2]
  • Ohmic heating is a method in which electric current is passed through food, causing internal
  • heat generation due to electrical resistance. This results in rapid and uniform heating.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Comment on lyophilization. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Comment on lyophilization. [K] / [CO5]
  • Lyophilization, also known as freeze drying, is a process where water is removed from frozen
  • material by sublimation under vacuum. It helps in preserving nutritional quality, flavor, and
  • structure.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define rheology. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Define rheology. [K] / [CO4]
  • Rheology is the study of the flow and deformation of materials, particularly fluids and semi
  • solids. It is important in understanding the behavior of food products during processing.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: State the methods to reduce water activity in foods. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• State the methods to reduce water activity in foods. [K] / [CO3]
  • Water activity in foods can be reduced by drying, addition of solutes such as salt or sugar,
  • freezing, and concentration. These methods inhibit microbial growth and enhance
  • preservation.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is the condition for an adiabatic process? / [CO3] [2x10 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the condition for an adiabatic process? [U] / [CO3]
  • An adiabatic process is one in which there is no heat exchange between the system and its
  • surroundings. The condition is that heat transfer (Q) is equal to zero.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the construction and working of a scraped surface heat exchanger. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the construction and working of a scraped surface heat exchanger. [U] /
  • [CO2]
  • A scraped surface heat exchanger consists o f a cylindrical shell with a rotating shaft fitted
  • with blades. The blades continuously scrape the inner surface to prevent fouling and ensure
  • efficient heat transfer. It is widely used for viscous and heat sensitive food products.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe surface tension and explain its importance in food processing operations. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe surface ten sion and explain its importance in food processing operations.
  • [U] / [CO4]
  • Surface tension is the force acting at the surface of a liquid due to cohesive forces between
  • molecules. It plays a significant role in emulsification, foaming, droplet formation, and
  • stability of food systems.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a short note on equipments used for size reduction of liquid foods. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a short note on equipments used for size reduction of liquid foods. [A] / [CO5]
  • Equipments such as homogenizers and colloid mills are used for size reduction of liquid
  • foods. These devices reduce particle size, impr ove texture, and enhance stability of
  • emulsions.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain rotary pumps. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain rotary pumps. [U] / [CO4]
  • Rotary pumps are positive displacement pumps that use rotating components to move fluids.
  • They are suitable for handling viscous and shear sensitive food materials and provide a steady
  • flow.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Differentiate First and Second Laws of Thermodynamics. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate First and Second Laws of Thermodynamics. [An] / [CO3]
  • The first law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed but can be transformed from
  • one form to another. The second law states that heat flows from a hi gher temperature to a
  • lower temperature and that entropy of an isolated system increases.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a short note on emissivity and its role in radiation heat transfer. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a short note on emissivity and its role in radiation heat transfer. [An] / [CO2]
  • Emissivity is the ability of a surface to emit thermal radiation compared t o a perfect black
  • body. It influences the efficiency of heat transfer in processes such as baking and drying.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain U-tube manometer. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain U-tube manometer. [U] / [CO4]
  • A U-tube manometer is a device used to measure pressure differences using a liquid column.
  • The difference in liquid levels in the two arms indicates the pressure difference.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Compare pasteurization and sterilization based on thermodynamic principles. / [CO3] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare pasteurization and sterilization based on thermodynamic principles. [An] /
  • [CO3]
  • Pasteurization involves heating food to moderate temperatures to destroy pathogenic
  • microorganisms, whereas sterilization involves higher temperatures to eliminate all
  • microorganisms including spores. Sterilization requires greater energy input.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain basic drying process with drying rate curve and stages. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain basic drying process with drying rate curve and stages. [An] / [CO5]
  • Drying is the process of removing moisture from food using heat. The drying rate curve
  • consists of three stages: initial constant rate period, falling rate period, and final equilibrium
  • stage. Moisture removal initially occurs rapidly and then decreases as bound water remains.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the concepts of internal energy and enthalpy and explain their significance in food processing operations. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the concepts of internal energy and enthalpy and explain their significance
  • in food processing operations. [An] / [CO3]
  • Internal energy is the total energy contained within a system, including kinetic and potential
  • energy of molecules. Enthalpy is the total heat content of a system and is given by H = U +
  • PV. These concepts are important in designing heating and cooling processes.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Compare natural convection and forced convection with respect to mechanism, heat transfer coefficient, and applications in food processing. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare natural convection and forced convection with respect to mechanism, heat
  • transfer coefficient, and applications in food processing. [U] / [CO2]
  • Natural convection occurs due to density differences caused by temperature variation,
  • whereas forced convection involves external forces such as pumps or fans. Forced convection
  • has a higher heat transfer coefficient and is widely used in industrial processes.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.solution_html:
• Derive the continuity equation. [C] / [CO4]
  • The continuity equation is derived from the principle o f conservation of mass. For a steady
  • flow system, the mass flow rate remains constant, expressed as ρA ₁ V₁ = ρA ₂ V₂ . It is
  • used in fluid flow analysis.
